methodological_rigor.justification: The study triangulates evidence across a 114-sample patient cohort (SCANDARE), ex vivo tumor-on-chip assays with multiple patient-derived ECM-myCAFs, two TNBC cell lines (MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-436), two cytotoxics (doxorubicin, paclitaxel), a specificity control (CAP fibroblasts), scRNA-seq, pan-kinase profiling, siRNA silencing (G0S2), and pharmacologic SRC inhibition (dasatinib). Statistical choices are appropriate (Shapiro–Wilk-driven selection, two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum and matched-pair signed-rank, Kolmogorov–Smirnov, Pearson χ2) with normalization and SEM reporting. Weaknesses include absence of a prospective power calculation, limited biological replicates for some ToC assays (n=2 patient-derived CAFs in MDA-MB-436 doxorubicin arm, n=2 for dasatinib G0S2 quantification), no blinded scoring statement for image analyses, lack of in vivo validation (no mouse experiments), and multiplicity correction is not described for the pan-kinase and TF-regulon screens.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The mechanistic core (ToC coculture, siRNA, kinase inhibition, scRNA-seq) is preclinical/ex vivo and the human component is a retrospective bulk-RNA-seq deconvolution study without clinical endpoints such as OS/PFS—so Oxford LoE maps to 5. Clinical relevance is nonetheless high: TNBC chemoresistance is a defined unmet need, the mechanism identifies dasatinib (an FDA-approved SRC inhibitor) as a repurposing opportunity to resensitize to doxorubicin, and G0S2 is proposed as a candidate biomarker/target with a plausible near-term translational path. Findings are directly actionable for combination-trial design in TNBC, though patient-level survival outcomes and in vivo pharmacology are not demonstrated.

reporting_quality.justification: No single standard applies cleanly; the mixed mechanistic/observational design was assessed against general bioscience reporting norms (and REMARK/STROBE items where relevant). Methods are thorough: ethics approval and trial registration (NCT03017573) for SCANDARE, defined RCB-based response definition, cell-line authentication (STR, mycoplasma, dated), extensive reagent catalog with RRIDs, detailed scRNA-seq preprocessing, and explicit image-analysis algorithms (STAMP, InceptionResNetV2). Omissions include no risk-of-bias discussion for the retrospective cohort, no CONSORT/PRISMA-style flow diagram of patient inclusion, and limited information on blinded/randomized acquisition. In the blinded manuscript no data-availability statement is visible (GEO/Zenodo accessions, deposited code) and the custom STAMP/CNN pipeline is not shared via a public repository identifier, reducing reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: ECM-myCAF has been previously described by this group in the immunotherapy-resistance context (ref 10) and CAFs are known to drive chemoresistance generically (ref 29), limiting conceptual novelty of the population itself. However, the manuscript delivers several genuinely novel pieces: the specific linkage of ECM-myCAF to chemotherapy (not immunotherapy) resistance in TNBC, identification of G0S2 as a required effector of CAF-mediated chemoprotection (previously unreported in therapy resistance), the SRC-family-kinase→TF→G0S2 cascade, and the early-timepoint spatial 'kiss-of-life' priming concept quantified by a CNN-based proximity analytic in ToC. Methodological novelty is moderate (ToC with primary CAFs is established, including by the same team), making this a strong incremental-to-novel contribution rather than paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a logical introduction→methods→results→discussion flow, acronyms defined on first use (TNBC, CAF, ECM-myCAF, ToC, G0S2) and quantitatively grounded figure captions that specify replicate structure and statistical tests. Minor issues: the abstract redundantly repeats its opening summary paragraph verbatim, some sentences are long and dense (introduction paragraph 2), and discussion ventures into speculation on HGF/FGF2 ligand–receptor mediators without matching data. Figure captions are standalone-interpretable and the mechanistic schematic (Fig. 8) effectively integrates findings.

key_strengths: Multi-modal triangulation: 114-sample patient RNA-seq deconvolution, ex vivo ToC with primary patient-derived CAFs, scRNA-seq, kinome profiling, siRNA and pharmacologic perturbation
Specificity controls (CAP fibroblasts had no chemoprotective effect) and replication across two TNBC lines and two chemotherapeutics
Novel mechanistic cascade (ECM-myCAF → SRC family kinases → TFs → G0S2 → apoptosis resistance) with convergent rescue by dasatinib and G0S2 silencing
CNN-based proximity analytics defining an early-time 'kiss-of-life' priming concept, with quantified distance/IOU correlates of cancer-cell fate
Clinically actionable repurposing hypothesis (dasatinib + doxorubicin) grounded in both patient cohort trends and ex vivo rescue
key_concerns: No in vivo (murine) validation of the SRC/G0S2 axis or dasatinib combination
Modest replicate counts in several ToC arms (n=2 patient-derived CAFs for MDA-MB-436 doxorubicin, dasatinib G0S2 quantification) and no formal power calculation
No visible data-availability statement, GEO/code deposition, or sharing of the custom STAMP/CNN pipeline in the blinded text
Mechanism linking ECM-myCAF secreted factors to SRC activation is speculative (HGF/FGF2 inferred from scRNA-seq ligand/receptor expression, not functionally demonstrated)
Retrospective cohort lacks a risk-of-bias assessment and formal multivariable adjustment of fibroblast proportion by stage/age/stromal content
Multiplicity correction not described for pan-kinase (~350 kinases) and TF-regulon screens
chief_reviewer.rationale: A rigorous, hypothesis-generating-plus-perturbation mechanistic study with convergent patient-cohort and ex vivo evidence identifying a tractable new axis (ECM-myCAF/SRC/G0S2) in TNBC chemoresistance; novelty, rigor, and clinical actionability warrant Tier 2 placement, but absence of in vivo validation and unshared data/code preclude Tier 1 and call for minor revisions.
